{
  "title": "Research Brief: Feature Ideas for Researcher Note-Taking Apps",
  "brief": [
    "Approach 1 (Networked Thought): Bidirectional linking and atomic notes to surface emergent connections across literature.",
    "Approach 2 (Structured Schemas): Metadata-heavy architectures featuring strict schema validation, citation tracking, and PDF field extraction.",
    "Approach 3 (AI Synthesis): RAG-driven semantic embeddings to auto-cluster related source documents and highlight contradictory claims.",
    "Limitation 1 (Organizational Overhead): High curation friction causes the 'collector's fallacy,' where users hoard notes without synthesizing insights (commonly reported in UX research).",
    "Limitation 2 (Decontextualization): Over-atomizing notes isolates findings from their original methodological context, rendering snippets misleading.",
    "Mainstream Criticism: Interactive 3D knowledge graph visualizers serve primarily as aesthetic vanity features rather than effective retrieval tools.",
    "Adjacent Analogy: Software version control (Git)—treating research hypotheses like code branches with commit histories, diffs, and merge requests."
  ]
}
